name: Procurement Versus Maintenance Conflict
anti_triggers: maintenance maturity evidenced and aligned with procurement
replacement logic already discriminated against maintenance reality
physical_basis: Equipment stress, poor maintenance and weak operating discipline can make a procurement narrative look more attractive than it should be.
operational_basis: Teams may fund replacement because maintenance and operations evidence are weak, not because the equipment boundary is the true dominant problem.
financial_mechanism: Capital can be spent on new equipment while the real economics remain in maintenance execution, downtime or operating discipline.
typical_false_assumption: If procurement looks attractive, maintenance must already be bounded.
hypothesis: Procurement and maintenance logic may be in conflict, making replacement-first action inadmissible until maintenance reality is bounded.
rival_hypotheses: replacement is still the dominant lever after maintenance is bounded
downtime and reliability burden are minor
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: maintenance weakness materially explains the visible burden
falsification_conditions: maintenance maturity is evidenced and sufficient
replacement logic remains valid after maintenance review
downtime and reliability burden are immaterial
allowed_claim_language: Procurement may be targeting a secondary symptom if maintenance reality has not yet been bounded.
prohibited_claim_language: The right answer is equipment replacement.
stop_conditions: maintenance and replacement logic are bounded enough to rank the dominant lever
escalation_conditions: operations or maintenance leadership confirmation required if documentary evidence remains thin
claim_permissions_impact: block procurement-driven ROI framing without maintenance discrimination
example_outputs: The capital story may be a maintenance story in disguise.
tests: industrial bundles should admit this when replacement framing appears before maintenance maturity is bounded
pattern must remain bounded at L2
